title: Backflow report submission: confirm the owner and proof of filing
description: Submission responsibility must be explicit: the tester, contractor, owner, or portal may file the result.
prompt: Who owns the final report submission and how is it proven?
answer: Submission responsibility must be explicit: the tester, contractor, owner, or portal may file the result. The completed record pairs the right assembly with a passing or failed status and proof of delivery.
urgency: Do not transmit property or tester data through an unverified link. Escalate when the listed portal, account, or assembly does not match the official notice.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: The official issuer controls portal, format, and account requirements.
A tester report may need an owner action before it is accepted by the program.
Repair records and retests must remain linked to the original asset.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Establish the exact record
steps.body: Use the issuer website or notice to identify the authorized portal, email, or recipient.

steps.title: Define the specific scope
steps.body: Confirm property, assembly, tester, date, and result before submission.

steps.title: Prove the closeout
steps.body: Save confirmation, receipt, or correspondence and resolve rejections before the deadline.

safeChecks: Use the official contact to verify portal domains.
Keep the completed test form before uploading.

stopConditions: The portal is not linked by the issuing program.
The submitted report cannot be matched to the device on site.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
